nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edge occurrences on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, a directed cycle through $v$ is a nonempty walk from $v$ back to $v$ whose vertices, with $v$ counted once, are pairwise distinct. A loop at $v$ is a cycle with one edge.
nodes.title: Directed cycle in a weighted edge list

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edge occurrences, a rational number $\lambda$ is the minimum cycle mean when some directed cycle $C$ has mean weight $w(C)/|C| = \lambda$, the weight divided by the number of edges, and no directed cycle has a smaller mean weight. It is Karp's $\lambda^*$; it exists exactly when the digraph has a cycle.
nodes.title: Minimum cycle mean of a weighted edge list

nodes.summary: For a list of weighted edge occurrences, vertices $s$ and $v$ and a natural number $k$, an integer $x$ is the minimum weight of a walk with $k$ edges from $s$ to $v$ when some walk ("edge progression") with exactly $k$ edges from $s$ to $v$ has weight $x$ and none has a smaller weight. This is Karp's $F_k(v) = x$; when there is no such walk, $F_k(v) = \infty$ and no $x$ qualifies. Walks may repeat vertices and edges.
nodes.title: Minimum weight of a walk with $k$ edges

nodes.summary: Let a list of integer-weighted edge occurrences define a strongly connected digraph on $n$ vertices, let $\lambda^*$ be its minimum cycle mean, and let $s$ be any vertex. With $F_k(v)$ the minimum weight of a walk with $k$ edges from $s$ to $v$, where a vertex with $F_n(v) = \infty$ contributes $+\infty$ to the minimum and an index with $F_k(v) = \infty$ contributes $-\infty$ to the maximum.
